summary: Tested /browse Extra Filters end-to-end (backend + frontend). Backend: 31/31 pytest tests PASS covering nationality regex, languages $all, string-stored numeric ranges (height/weight), categorical equality, yes/no toggles, composition with gender/city. Frontend: panel opens with 4 sections, filter selection correctly filters to Sophia only, apply button works, clear preserves city & gender, toggle closes panel, badge is gold (#C6A87C / rgb(198,168,124)). Provider detail page still renders Sophia's Essence characteristics. Mobile (390px) panel is single-column and usable. ONE suspected minor frontend bug: the Extra Filters count badge shows 2 when selecting hair_color + 1 language + tattoos (expected 3). Languages count may not contribute to the badge, or the language pill click is not updating state reliably in Playwright (hard to confirm visually since hair_color=Brunette alone returns only Sophia).

ui_bugs.issue: Active extra-filter count badge appears to not include the 'languages' selection. Selecting hair_color=Brunette + French pill + tattoos=no showed badge='2' instead of expected '3'. Separate test clicking only French pill showed no badge at all. Either the language pill's toggleLang state update isn't firing, or the activeExtraCount formula is not counting languages as expected.

issues: Console warning: 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' and '<span> cannot be a child of <select>' — hydration-error source unclear but worth auditing the SiteHeader/Browse SELECT/OPTION markup (likely cosmetic).

action_items: Investigate the activeExtraCount badge: verify (filters.languages || []).length > 0 branch actually contributes. Quick repro — load /browse, open Extra Filters, click only the 'French' language pill, observe badge does not appear.
Optional: audit the <span>-in-<option>/<select> React hydration warning seen in console on /browse.
critical_code_review_comments: Gender is stored lowercase ('female') in Sophia's profile and frontend sends lowercase — backend does case-sensitive equality match on 'gender' field. Acceptable because pills produce a closed set, but any admin/seed entering 'Female' (capitalised) will be silently unfilterable. Consider normalising gender storage or using case-insensitive regex like nationality.
_add_numeric_range_expr correctly uses $expr + $toDouble to handle string-stored heights/weights; works but the query cannot use indexes. Fine for current scale (33 providers).

EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS in Browse.js omits 'languages' deliberately (it's an array), and activeExtraCount adds +1 for it via a separate clause — consider unifying by using a single derivation function to avoid the bug pattern suspected above.
Browse.js has grown large (~336 lines) with inline gender buttons repeated 4x — extract a <GenderPill> component for DRY.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_browse_filters.py covers all 15 physical-characteristic filters with 31 tests — re-run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_browse_filters.py -v` after any provider-filter change. The lone suspected frontend bug is isolated to the language-pill badge contribution; everything else (filter application, clear behaviour, toggle, mobile layout, provider detail page) verified working end-to-end.
rca of the issue: Language pill badge bug — Candidate root cause: in Browse.js `activeExtraCount` is computed synchronously from `filters.languages`, but if toggleLang's setFilters call is being batched or state shape mismatches (e.g. languages stored as undefined instead of []), the +1 branch evaluates to 0. Reproduction: visit /browse → click 'Extra Filters' → click ONLY the 'French' pill → observe no badge. Mitigation: add a console.log in toggleLang to confirm state updates, and/or change formula to include `languages` key inside EXTRA_FILTER_KEYS with a specialised length check.
